text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: dedicated pool `dedicated-acme-west-2` reporting allocation failures for tenant `acme-corp` (err=NoAvailableDevices). Severity: P0. Auto-page to oncall.
Maya R.: I see it. Dashboard shows pool capacity 24/24 GPUs used. Spike in batched requests from acme at 2026-01-09T14:12Z.
Jorge (oncall): I'm taking primary. Priya please stay for infra, Alex for product/contact constraints. Maya keep runtime.
Priya S.: grabbing logs from pool manager: ```
[2026-01-09T14:12:07Z] pool=dedicated-acme-west-2 tenant=acme-corp allocate request=rt-32g no-devices
[2026-01-09T14:12:08Z] scheduler: running=24 queued=6 max_capacity=24
[2026-01-09T14:12:10Z] gpu-orchestrator: allocation-failure tenant=acme-corp reason=reserved_exhausted
```
Alex T.: contract note: acme paid for isolated reserved pool, explicit no-burst clause. They have dedicated KMS and private subnet.
Maya R.: quick mitigation ideas: 1) throttle heavy batch endpoints for acme 2) reduce batch size and limit concurrency server-side 3) temporarily re-route low-priority acme jobs to a quantized variant on same pool (if memory allows) 4) emergency add nodes to pool 5) request permission for controlled burst into shared with envelope encryption.
customer-ops-bot: Customer `acme-corp` has posted: "We are seeing 500s across our inference calls, major impact to customers. Please update ETA."
Jorge (oncall): Communicating to acme: "We're investigating. Short mitigation may include limiting batch size and adding capacity. ETA for node add ~20 min, will confirm."
Priya S.: infra note: we have 6 idle A100s in region but they're not pre-allocated for dedicated pools. Manual allocation requires infra ticket + image sync. Historically ~15-25min.
Alex T.: product/legal: we must not burst without explicit written consent from acme. I can message their contract owner now.
Maya R.: runtime tweak: we can drop model to `gpt-large-8bit` for realtime route which cuts memory by ~30% and may free 6-8 slots. Risk: quality impact. Can roll as canary.
Jorge (oncall): Proposed plan: short-term apply per-route throttling to free capacity for critical low-latency traffic + canary model degrade for realtime routes. Parallel track: request emergency node add. Ask acme for fast approval for shared-burst only if needed.
Priya S.: issuing infra emergency request INF-9011 for +4 A100. Pinged infra lead.
Alex T.: I sent acme legal a DM asking for explicit permission for emergency shared-burst if we can't regain capacity. Waiting reply.
Maya R.: applying throttles now: ```
redwood-cli routing set-rate --tenant acme-corp --route /v1/batch_generate --qps 40% --reason "emergency capacity"
```
Maya R.: canary deploy model degrade for realtime: ```
redwood-cli deploy-model --tenant acme-corp --from gpt-large-v3 --to gpt-large-v3-8bit --routes /v1/realtime --canary 10% --ttl 15m
```
Priya S.: infra update: lead acknowledged, provisioning nodes. ETA ~12 min. Ticket INF-9011.
customer-ops-bot: acme: "Thanks, please avoid moving data out of our VPC. 8bit OK for 10-15m as long as we get notif when rolled back."
Alex T.: acknowledged to customer: "No data will leave your VPC. 8bit canary will be used only for a subset of traffic. We'll notify when rollback occurs."
Jorge (oncall): Monitor: telemetry shows 30% drop in queued requests after throttle + canary. Error rate lowered from 6.8% -> 2.1% in 3 minutes.
Maya R.: logs show freed allocation slots after canary: ```
[2026-01-09T14:18:45Z] runtime: freed 3 gpus (model_degrade) tenant=acme-corp
[2026-01-09T14:19:02Z] scheduler: running=21 queued=2
```
Priya S.: infra: new nodes are booting. Container images syncing. ETA node ready ~9min.
Alex T.: product action: schedule post-incident review to propose fallback clause: 'emergency sealed-burst' that keeps data in tenant-controlled encryption envelope so legal allows temporary mixed tenancy.
Jorge (oncall): decision log: DO NOT AUTO-BURST. ACTIONS NOW = [throttle applied, model canary, infra node add requested, contact acme]. If infra confirm add <15min and error <1% we'll downgrade severity.
Priya S.: nodes ready and agents connected: ```
[2026-01-09T14:28:01Z] node-fleet-72 joined pool dedicated-acme-west-2
[2026-01-09T14:29:12Z] runtime: agent connected, scheduling enabled
```
Maya R.: scheduler now shows capacity 28 max, running=21. Headroom regained. Error rate fell to 0.4%.
customer-ops-bot: acme: "We see successful responses now, thank you. Please confirm whether any data touched shared services."
Alex T.: reply to acme: "No shared-burst occurred. Added dedicated nodes only. We will follow up with a post-incident note and options for future capacity protection."
Jorge (oncall): Closing page if metrics stable for 15m. Postmortem owners: Maya (runtime), Priya (infra), Alex (product). Action items: 1) shorten emergency node add time <10m, 2) product to propose sealed emergency-burst contract term, 3) automated soft-degrade path for reserved pools.
Maya R.: will collect logs and KV cache snapshots to validate no tenant leakage.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INF-9011 completed, +4 GPUs added. Error rate now 0.35%. Monitoring window started.
Jorge (oncall): closing active page. Leaving channel open for 30m. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
